name: Basilica di Santa Maria in Montesanto, Chiesa degli Artisti
html:
Basilica di Santa Maria in Montesanto – Chiesa degli Artisti
Set in Rome’s iconic Piazza del Popolo, the historic Church of the Artists is a distinguished Baroque basilica renowned for its centuries-old heritage and unique connection with the worlds of art and culture. Home to the celebrated Messa degli Artisti, it provides an inspiring setting for a gathering dedicated to peace, trust and human flourishing.

name: Cancelleria Palace
html:
A Renaissance Masterpiece and Venue of Distinction

The Palazzo della Cancelleria, or Palace of the Chancellery, stands as a seminal example of Renaissance architecture and a historical jewel in Rome’s rich tapestry. Commissioned by Cardinal Riario and constructed between 1485 and 1513, this grand palace was the first building in Rome to be erected from the ground up in the new Renaissance style, marking a significant departure from medieval architectural traditions.

The Palazzo’s imposing and elegant façade envelops the small Basilica di San Lorenzo in Damaso, seamlessly integrating the church into its grand design. The palace’s design, characterized by its harmonious proportions and innovative use of space, exemplifies the Renaissance ideals of symmetry and classical grandeur. The façade’s majestic lines and ornate detailing are emblematic of the era’s artistic and architectural revolution.

One of the palace’s most notable features is the Sala dei Cento Giorni, or Hall of One Hundred Days. This stunning chamber is renowned for its breathtaking mural, completed by the celebrated artist Giorgio Vasari in a mere 100 days—a feat of remarkable speed and skill. Vasari’s achievement, which he proudly shared with Michelangelo, is immortalized in the room’s title. Michelangelo’s famous response, “Si vede” (“It shows”), reflects the mural’s exceptional quality and the profound impact it left on the art world.

Today, the Sala dei Cento Giorni serves as a prestigious venue for distinguished events and gatherings. The Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation (IASC) is honored to host one of its most respected events in this historically and artistically significant space, thanks to the support of the Administration of the Patrimony of the Apostolic See (APSA). The grandeur of the Palazzo della Cancelleria and its beautifully appointed Sala dei Cento Giorni provide a fitting backdrop for events that seek to blend historical reverence with contemporary intellectual discourse.

The Palazzo della Cancelleria remains a testament to the enduring legacy of Renaissance art and architecture, offering a timeless setting for the exchange of ideas and the celebration of cultural heritage.

name: Church of San Silvestro al Quirinale
html:
The Church of San Silvestro al Quirinale, located in the Trevi district, has ancient origins dating back to the 9th-11th centuries, when it was known as “in Biberatica” due to its proximity to Via Biberatica.

The history of this sacred building is marked by renovations, modifications, and changes in management, entrusted to various religious orders.

In 1507, Pope Julius II granted custody of the church to the Dominicans of the Congregation of San Marco, who promoted the reconstruction of the single-nave plan with two chapels on each side, a dome, and a deep presbytery, as well as the construction of the adjoining convent. In 1555, the church passed to the Theatines, who made it a training house for novices, and a campaign to renovate the façade and interior decoration was launched. Three centuries later, San Silvestro al Quirinale was purchased by the state and used as the headquarters of the Military Engineers. It was subsequently converted into a barracks until, following the widening and lowering of the street level toward Via Nazionale, it returned to its sacred role. The façade and two chapels were demolished during this period, along with a nine-meter drop that created a “floating” effect within the church.

name: Dubai, United Arab Emirates
html:
In a city where the future is built every day, Dubai emerged as the perfect host for the World Changers Summit, in collaboration with AIMS Dubai — a global gathering of visionary leaders, innovators, and changemakers determined to shape a better world.

Rising from the golden sands of the Arabian Desert, Dubai is more than a modern metropolis; it is a living testament to transformation, resilience, and bold imagination. From the towering heights of the Burj Khalifa, the tallest structure in the world, to the visionary innovation hubs of Dubai Future Foundation and Museum of the Future, the city pulses with an energy uniquely suited to host a summit focused on global progress.

Home to over 200 nationalities, Dubai is a cultural mosaic where East meets West — a bridge between continents and a platform where ideas from around the world converge. The city’s architectural marvels, cutting-edge infrastructure, and deep-rooted heritage reflect a dual commitment: honoring tradition while driving innovation. Whether it’s the historic Al Fahidi district, the futuristic skyline of Downtown Dubai, or the thriving academic and research institutions such as Dubai Science Park and Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre, every corner of the city echoes the summit’s themes of sustainability, leadership, and purpose-driven impact.

Dubai’s role as a global hub for diplomacy, commerce, and humanitarian progress made it more than a backdrop — it became an active force in the summit experience Just as the city itself evolved from a desert trading post into a global center of vision and possibility, the World Changers Summit in Dubai became a call to action — inviting participants to think beyond convention, challenge the status quo, and transform bold ideas into tangible impact.

Dubai isn’t just a city that rises — it leads by example. And within that spirit of progress, we at WCS were honored to contribute to a new chapter in the global story of change.

name: Explorer Club New York
html:
Nestled in the heart of Manhattan’s Upper East Side, The Explorers Club is a historic institution and headquarters for the world’s most daring adventurers, scientists, and explorers. Founded in 1904, the Club has supported pioneering expeditions to the North and South Poles, Mount Everest, the depths of the ocean, and into outer space.

Set inside a stunning Jacobean revival townhouse, the Club features grand wood-paneled halls, mounted artifacts from legendary expeditions, a vast research library, and a rich collection of relics — from moon rocks to tribal totems. The ambiance reflects both intellectual curiosity and a deep reverence for the unknown.

Whether hosting a lecture on climate change, a black-tie gala for Arctic researchers, or a meeting of modern-day space scientists, The Explorers Club remains a vibrant hub of discovery and inspiration — where past meets future in the spirit of exploration.

name: The Lateran Apostolic Palace
html:
The Lateran Apostolic Palace, situated in the heart of Rome, stands as one of the most distinguished and revered locations within the Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation (IASC). This historic edifice is not merely a venue but a living testament to the rich tapestry of the Church’s history, where the interplay of art, faith, and heritage creates a profound and captivating experience for all who visit.

Dating back to the early days of Christianity, the Lateran Apostolic Palace has long been a symbol of the Church’s enduring legacy and spiritual authority. It is the official ecclesiastical residence of the Pope and the principal seat of the Holy See, embodying centuries of theological scholarship, artistic achievement, and historical significance. The grandeur of its architecture and the exquisite artistry of its interiors reflect the deep spiritual and cultural heritage of the Catholic Church.

As visitors traverse its magnificent halls and chambers, they are enveloped in an atmosphere that transcends time, experiencing firsthand the harmonious blend of sacred art and architectural splendor. The palace is adorned with priceless frescoes, intricate mosaics, and masterful sculptures, each piece narrating the story of faith and devotion through the ages. The elegance of its Renaissance and Baroque decorations, combined with the solemnity of its sacred spaces, creates an environment where the divine and the artistic converge.

The Lateran Apostolic Palace’s significance is further amplified by its role in the vision of Pope Francis, who, in his capacity as Bishop of Rome, has ardently sought to elevate this historic site as a beacon of faith, culture, and beauty. His vision encompasses a profound desire to use this sacred space to foster a deeper appreciation for the Church’s rich heritage and to inspire reflection and dialogue on matters of faith and human experience.

This extraordinary palace not only serves as a custodian of the Church’s history but also as a vibrant center for contemporary dialogue and cultural engagement. It continues to be a source of inspiration, wonder, and wisdom for generations, embodying the Church’s commitment to bridging the past and the present in a meaningful and impactful way.

The Lateran Apostolic Palace, with its majestic presence and historical depth, offers a unique and enriching journey through the heart of the Church’s legacy, making it an essential destination for those seeking to understand and appreciate the profound intersection of faith, art, and culture.

name: Maison Assouline
html:
Maison Assouline is Assouline’s flagship boutique, restaurant and piano bar, in the prestigious Bujairi Terrace in Riyadh. This destination showcases Assouline’s commitment to luxury and culture in a setting inspired by Riyadh’s rich heritage.

Discover the latest Assouline releases, rare first editions of classic titles, and more within the thoughtfully designed two story space. For those looking to take in the scenery, the outdoor terrace overlooking Diriyah is the perfect setting. Maison Assouline Riyadh is a cultural destination, offering a meticulously curated environment that celebrates the art of living well.

name: Monte Carlo
html: Montecarlo is a refined, versatile brand known for blending timeless style with dependable quality. Designed for people who appreciate clean lines, premium materials, and everyday comfort, Montecarlo offers pieces that feel elevated without being complicated. From the first touch to long-term wear, each detail reflects careful craftsmanship and a focus on lasting performance—making Montecarlo a confident choice for those who want elegance, practicality, and reliability in one.

name: Palace of Brigadave
html:
The Palace of Brigades is one of the most prestigious and historically significant landmarks in Tirana. Nestled among lush greenery on the outskirts of the city, this grand complex was originally constructed in the 1930s during the reign of King Zog I as a royal residence. Designed with a blend of Italian architectural influence and Albanian elegance, the palace later became a central venue for official state functions during the communist era.

Today, the Palace of Brigades serves as an important ceremonial site, hosting government receptions, diplomatic events, and high-profile gatherings. Its spacious halls, refined interiors, and surrounding gardens create an atmosphere of formality and sophistication, making it a symbol of Albania’s political history and cultural heritage.

name: Polytechnic University of Tirana
address: Polytechnic University of Tirana, Tirana, Albania, Albania
html: The Polytechnic University of Tirana is one of Albania’s leading institutions for engineering, architecture, and applied sciences, located in the heart of Tirana. Known for its strong academic tradition and technical focus, the university plays a key role in shaping the country’s future professionals in fields such as civil engineering, information technology, and environmental studies. Its campus combines a classic academic atmosphere with modern research facilities, attracting students from across the nation who seek a practical, career-oriented education. Beyond academics, it serves as a hub for innovation and collaboration, contributing significantly to Albania’s technological and infrastructural development.

name: Porto Palermo, Albania
html: Porto Palermo is one of Albania’s most breathtaking hidden gems — a quiet bay where crystal-clear Ionian waters meet dramatic cliffs and centuries-old history. Just south of Himara, this small peninsula is crowned by the impressive Ali Pasha Castle, offering panoramic views over the sea. With its untouched nature, peaceful beaches, and turquoise waters, Porto Palermo is perfect for travelers seeking both beauty and tranquility away from the crowds.

name: Princess Salons of Palazzo Brancaccio
html:
A Historic Residence of Art, Culture, and Innovation

Palazzo Brancaccio, the last princely residence built in Rome, stands as a masterpiece of elegance and cultural refinement. Located on Via Merulana 248, between the Esquiline Hill and the Domus Aurea of Emperor Nero, the palace was commissioned in the late 19th century by Mary Elizabeth Field Brancaccio and designed by renowned architects Gaetano Koch and Luca Carimini.

Throughout its history, Palazzo Brancaccio has served as a symbol of the harmonious dialogue between history and modernity — a place where art, intellect, and society converge. Its grand halls and ornate frescoes reflect the splendor of a bygone era, while its continued role as a venue for cultural and academic gatherings connects the past to the future.

At the heart of the residence lies the celebrated “Saloni della Principessa” (Princess Salons) — a collection of opulent rooms once home to Princess Donna Fernanda Brancaccio. Adorned with gilded ceilings, crystal chandeliers, and exquisite artworks, these salons today host distinguished international events, conferences, and gala evenings that celebrate creativity, knowledge, and human achievement.

As the venue of the World Changers Summit and the Transcendence Book Premiere Presentation, Palazzo Brancaccio continues its legacy as a living testament to the enduring dialogue between culture and progress — where the elegance of history meets the vision of innovation.

name: KSSO, Saudi Arabia
address: The King Salman Science Oasis (KSSO), Riyadh
html: The King Salman Science Oasis (KSSO) is a major interactive, non-profit science center located in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, opened around 2022 to promote STEM education. It features over 100 interactive exhibits, a 3D dome theater, and STEAM academies, supporting Saudi Vision 2030 by inspiring innovation in science, technology, and sustainability.

name: Skopje
address: Skopje, North Macedonia, Skopje, North Macedonia, 1000, Balkan
html:
Skopje, the capital and largest city of North Macedonia, is situated in the heart of the Balkan Peninsula. The city is a fascinating mix of old and new, with its historical roots dating back to the Roman and Byzantine eras. Skopje’s skyline is marked by the ancient Stone Bridge, which connects the Ottoman-era Old Bazaar to the modern part of the city.

The city underwent significant reconstruction after the 1963 earthquake, leading to a blend of Brutalist architecture and contemporary designs. Skopje is also known for its ambitious Skopje 2014 project, which aimed to give the city a more classical appeal with numerous statues and neoclassical buildings.

Culturally, Skopje boasts a lively arts scene with numerous galleries, theaters, and the Macedonian Opera and Ballet. The city is also famous for its vibrant festivals, including the Skopje Jazz Festival and the International Balkan Festival. The Old Bazaar is a hub for traditional crafts and local cuisine, offering a unique glimpse into the region’s history and cultural heritage.

Skopje’s diverse culinary scene reflects its multicultural influences, with a mix of Macedonian, Turkish, and Mediterranean flavors. The city’s nightlife is equally diverse, with a range of bars, clubs, and live music venues that cater to all tastes.

Surrounded by picturesque landscapes, including the Matka Canyon and the Vodno Mountain, Skopje offers numerous outdoor activities for nature enthusiasts. The Millennium Cross on Mount Vodno provides a panoramic view of the city and is a popular destination for both locals and tourists.

In summary, Skopje is a city of contrasts and connections, where history meets modernity, and cultural diversity is celebrated in every corner.

name: Spartanburg, South Carolina
html:
A Reflective Gathering in the Heart of the American South

Spartanburg, South Carolina, offered in partnership with the World Changers Summit and in celebration of Elysian’s 10-year anniversary, presents a truly meaningful setting — where culture, heritage, and empowerment intersect in a space designed for deep reflection and transformative dialogue.

Nestled in the soulful landscape of the American South, Spartanburg is more than a geographic destination; it is a place where the spirit of community, creativity, and history converge. Known for its legacy in textile innovation and its evolving cultural landscape, the city provides a backdrop of quiet strength — ideal for honoring the profound impact of women leaders and changemakers across the world.

This exclusive gathering, co-hosted by World Changers Summit, brings together visionaries in a city that embodies resilience and reinvention. Spartanburg’s tranquil charm and cultural richness invite guests into a serene environment where voices are amplified, stories are honored, and leadership is redefined. From historic mills repurposed into artistic venues, to vibrant community spaces rooted in diversity and inclusion, the city reflects the very essence of Elysian’s mission.

Within this carefully curated experience, attendees are invited to engage in dialogue that transcends borders and ideologies. The stillness of the surroundings, paired with the warmth of Southern hospitality, offers a grounding space to reflect on progress, purpose, and the shared path forward. Whether walking the halls of Chapman Cultural Center or gathering beneath the canopy of Southern pines, every moment is designed to awaken thought, connection, and a deeper sense of meaning.

Spartanburg is not just a host, but a participant — a city whose evolving identity mirrors the journey of women who lead with vision, compassion, and power. Through this partnership, the World Changers Summit continues its global mission of shaping the future by elevating the voices that matter most.

In essence, Spartanburg offers more than a location; it offers an atmosphere — one of clarity, inspiration, and grounded transformation. Here, in a setting where history and hope meet, the 10-year celebration of Elysian becomes not just an event, but a living tribute to the enduring influence of women and the future they are shaping.

name: St. Moritz Switzerland
html: Set amidst the breathtaking Swiss Alps, St. Moritz offers a rare blend of natural majesty, cultural depth, and timeless elegance — the perfect stage for the World Changer Summit. Known as the birthplace of Alpine winter tourism and twice host of the Winter Olympics, this historic resort town in the Engadin Valley is renowned for its pristine lakes, sun-drenched peaks, and refined lifestyle. With over 3,000 years of history, multilingual heritage (Romansh, German, Italian), and a calendar full of world-class events like White Turf and the Snow Polo World Cup, St. Moritz inspires innovation while honoring tradition. Its unique energy, where luxury meets legacy, makes it more than a destination — it becomes part of the experience. As we gather to shape the future at WCS, St. Moritz stands not only as our backdrop, but as a living symbol of excellence, resilience, and visionary thinking.

name: The Pontifical Academy of Sciences
address: The Pontifical Academy of Sciences Casina Pio IV, Vatican, Vatican City, Vatican
html:
A Beacon of Knowledge and Inquiry

The Pontifical Academy of Sciences (Latin: Pontificia Academia Scientiarum) stands as a premier institution of scientific and intellectual excellence within the Vatican City, embodying the intersection of faith and reason. Established in 1936 by Pope Pius XI, the Academy is headquartered in the historic Casina Pio IV, nestled within the serene Vatican Gardens. This esteemed venue serves as the central hub for the Academy’s mission to advance the mathematical, physical, and natural sciences, while addressing profound epistemological questions.

The origins of the Academy trace back to the Accademia Pontificia dei Nuovi Lincei, founded in 1847, which itself was a direct successor to the illustrious Accademia dei Lincei. The latter was established in Rome in 1603 by the eminent botanist and naturalist Federico Cesi. Known as the “Academy of Lynxes,” it was a pioneering institution in the scientific community, with Galileo Galilei serving as its esteemed president. The lineage of these academies reflects a rich tradition of scientific inquiry and intellectual pursuit that continues to flourish under the Pontifical Academy of Sciences.

The Academy’s primary objective is to foster the advancement of scientific knowledge across various disciplines, including mathematics, physics, and the natural sciences. It is dedicated to exploring the fundamental principles of the universe and promoting scholarly research that bridges the realms of science and philosophy. Through its rigorous research programs and scholarly activities, the Academy contributes significantly to the global scientific community and offers a unique perspective on the relationship between scientific discovery and ethical considerations.

The Casina Pio IV, the Academy’s headquarters, is a symbol of the harmonious blend of historical legacy and modern scientific inquiry. This architectural gem, situated in the tranquil Vatican Gardens, provides an inspiring backdrop for the Academy’s work, reflecting the serene yet profound nature of scientific exploration.

The Pontifical Academy of Sciences not only celebrates its historical heritage but also embraces contemporary challenges and opportunities in the scientific world. Its commitment to advancing knowledge and fostering interdisciplinary dialogue underscores its pivotal role in shaping the future of science and its ethical implications.

As the main venue for the Institute for Advanced Studies and Cooperation (IASC), the Pontifical Academy of Sciences stands as a beacon of intellectual curiosity and scholarly excellence. It continues to inspire and engage with the global scientific community, bridging the ancient traditions of inquiry with the forefront of contemporary scientific advancements.

name: Vatican Museums
html:
Inspirational Private Visit to Vatican Museums
The Vatican Museums, an unparalleled destination ofered by the Institute for Advanced Study and Cooperation, offer an extraordinary experience for private visits, where tranquility and beauty converge to create an atmosphere of profound reflection. Nestled within the heart of Vatican City, these museums are renowned not only for their breathtaking art collections but also for their serene ambiance that provides a peaceful escape from the bustling world outside.

As one of the most stunning cultural landmarks globally, the Vatican Museums are a sanctuary where silence and serenity enhance the appreciation of an unparalleled artistic heritage. Visitors are invited to explore this majestic venue in an exclusive setting, where the hushed reverence of the environment allows for a deeply personal connection with the masterpieces on display.

Organized by the Institute for Advanced Study and Cooperation, these private tours offer a unique opportunity to experience the Vatican Museums in a way that few others can. The serene and contemplative atmosphere, coupled with the museum’s stunning architectural grandeur and exceptional art collections, provides an intimate and immersive experience. Each visit is tailored to reflect the specific interests of the guests, ensuring a deeply engaging and enriching encounter with art and history.

The Vatican Museums are home to an extensive collection that spans centuries of artistic achievement. From the iconic frescoes of the Sistine Chapel, painted by Michelangelo, to the elegant Raphael Rooms and the captivating sculptures in the Pio-Clementine Museum, the museums offer a voyage through the heights of artistic and spiritual expression. Each gallery and artifact tells a story of profound cultural significance, and the quiet of private visits allows for a contemplative appreciation of these masterpieces.

The quiet elegance of the Vatican Museums transforms the art experience into a journey of reflection and inspiration. The serene environment of the museums enhances the contemplative nature of the visit, allowing guests to fully absorb the beauty and significance of the works displayed. In this tranquil setting, the art is not merely observed but felt, resonating deeply within each visitor.

In summary, the Vatican Museums, as a premier destination of the Institute for Advanced Study and Cooperation, offer an exceptional experience where art, history, and tranquility intersect. The exclusive private visits provide an unparalleled opportunity to engage with some of the world’s most significant artistic treasures in a peaceful and introspective environment. Here, amid the grandeur of one of the world’s most beautiful settings, visitors find a serene haven that enriches both the mind and spirit.

name: Venus The Lateran University
address: Piazza San Giovanni in Laterano 4, Vatican City, 00184
html:
A Center of Academic Excellence and Formation

The Lateran University (Pontificia Universitas Lateranensis), often referred to as the “University of the Pope,” is a distinguished institution of higher learning located in Vatican City. Established in 1773, the university embodies a rich tradition of academic excellence, deeply rooted in the Catholic intellectual heritage. Its mission is to provide comprehensive education and formation in various disciplines, including theology, philosophy, law, and social sciences, while fostering a profound understanding of faith and reason.

The Lateran University operates under the auspices of the Holy See, offering a unique academic environment that integrates scholarly inquiry with spiritual formation. As the first university founded by the papacy, it holds a special place in the history of Catholic education, continually adapting to the evolving needs of society while remaining faithful to its core values.

The university’s curriculum is designed to cultivate critical thinking, ethical reasoning, and a commitment to service. Its esteemed faculty includes leading scholars and practitioners who guide students in exploring the complexities of contemporary issues through the lens of Catholic social teaching. The Lateran University encourages interdisciplinary dialogue, equipping its graduates to address the challenges of modern society with a holistic perspective.

Situated in a historical context, the university’s campus features beautiful architecture and serene surroundings that inspire both learning and reflection. It serves as a vibrant hub for intellectual engagement and spiritual growth, welcoming students from diverse backgrounds who seek to deepen their understanding of faith and its implications for society.

In its commitment to academic rigor and moral integrity, the Lateran University plays a vital role in shaping future leaders within the Church and beyond. Its emphasis on integrating faith with reason positions it as a significant contributor to the global discourse on ethics, social justice, and the common good.

As a prominent institution within Vatican City, the Lateran University not only preserves the rich tradition of Catholic education but also embraces contemporary challenges, preparing its students to make meaningful contributions to the world. Its ongoing dedication to fostering dialogue and understanding among different cultures and disciplines underscores its mission as a center of academic excellence and formation.
